title: Passive SI session (F2): risk is not escalated (no invented plan/intent/hospitalisation)
hypothesis: The note does not overstate risk beyond what was said.

data.note:
Subjective
Client reported that the week has been heavy since losing their job three weeks ago, stating they mostly stay in bed. Client endorsed passive suicidal ideation, reporting that some nights they think everyone would be better off without them and wishing they could just not wake up. Client denied having a plan or intent to end their life, identifying their son as a protective factor.

Objective
Not assessed this session regarding appearance, behaviour, speech, affect, thought process, and measure scores, aside from clinical observations of client reporting depressive symptoms and passive suicidal ideation.

Assessment
Client presents with moderate recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.1) complicated by recent job loss and increased depressive symptoms including psychomotor slowing (staying in bed) and passive suicidal ideation. Risk is currently mitigated by protective factors (son) and lack of intent or plan, as well as absence of access to firearms or stockpiled medications. Client demonstrated engagement in collaborative safety planning.

Plan
Update safety plan including brother Marcus as emergency contact and the 988 lifeline number Assign behavioral activation homework of walking the dog around the block once each morning Schedule follow-up individual therapy session for Thursday (increasing frequency to twice this week)
